Rationale.DE1_ResultFidelity: Demo-only replication case. Replicated demo outputs match the type of results demonstrated in the original: function vectors improve zero-shot performance (0%→26% antonym, 7.1%→83.3% country-capital), improve shuffled-label performance (30%→54%), and do not harm clean ICL (64%→62%). Directional effects are consistent with the paper. Absolute accuracy differences are explicitly acknowledged and explained by evaluation setup differences (sample size, filtering, seeds).
Rationale.DE2_ConclusionConsistency: Replicated conclusions are consistent with the original: both confirm function vectors enable zero-shot task transfer and demonstrate robustness across context changes. The replication correctly claims to demonstrate 'the core mechanism of function vectors.' No contradictory conclusions are made, and claims are appropriately limited to what was actually replicated (2 tasks, not 40+).
Rationale.DE3_NoExternalInformation: No external or hallucinated information detected. Paper reference (Todd et al., ICLR 2024) is from original CodeWalkthrough.md. Dataset counts verified (2398 antonym, 197 country-capital with minor 1-pair difference). Methodology details match original code. Paper-reported results (~90%, ~58%) match plan.md values. All claims traceable to original repo files or actual experimental outputs.
